newsitem.title: USA: Hilton results hurt by gambling losses, charges.
newsitem.headline: Hilton results hurt by gambling losses, charges.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp., the largest hotel and casino company in the United States, reported a fourth quarter loss Tuesday due to gambling losses and one-time charges.
The company reported a net loss of $68.6 million, or 33 cents a share, in the fourth quarter of 1996, after charges, compared with a profit of $63.1 million, or 32 cents a share, last year.

The latest quarter included a $74.1 million, one-time charge to acquire debt related to its $2 billion acquisition of Bally Entertainment Corp. Excluding the charge, Hilton would have reported a profit of $6 million, or 3 cents a share.

The company was hurt by losses at high rolling baccarat tables in Las Vegas, sluggish casino business elsewhere in Nevada, and charges for opening a riverboat casino in Missouri and moving one in Louisiana.

Earlier this month, Hilton warned investors of the fourth quarter losses and charges and after Tuesday's report, Hilton stock was off 50 cents at $26.125 on the New York Stock Exchange in late trading.
"Gaming was clearly a disappointment in 1996," Chief Executive Officer Stephen Bollenbach said in a statement.

He noted, however, the company was optimistic about the gambling business in 1997 as it integrates Bally Entertainment hotels and casinos with its operations and adds a new "Star Trek" attraction to the Las Vegas Hilton.
Hilton said the hotel side of its business performed well in the fourth quarter.
Hotel occupancy rose to 72 percent in 1996's fourth quarter vs. 71 percent last year, while the average room rate jumped 7 percent to $142 per night.

For the year, the company reported overall net income after charges of $81.7 million or 41 cents a share, on revenue of $1.9 billion vs. a net profit of 89 cents a share on sales of $1.65 billion in 1995.
